text:
Sam (AM): Quick question — Acme POC wants to buy through AWS Marketplace using a private offer but also expects our committed discount for a 12-month term. Can we align marketplace pricing with the direct commit price? They specifically asked that billing go through Marketplace (for their internal compliance).

Marie - DealDesk: Short answer: maybe. Marketplace private offers can reflect a discounted price, but there are caveats (metering, fees, revenue recognition). We need Finance + Marketplace Ops sign-off.

Ajay (SE): For the POC we'll need Dedicated capacity SKU for 8 vGPUs x2 weeks. If marketplace SKU won't support short-term reserved capacity, we can create a POC SKU with an expiry date. Also confirm model / token limits so we can size the pool.

Lia Finance: FYI marketplace takes ~12% transaction fee (varies by marketplace). If you want to match a direct commit price, we either: (a) increase the marketplace listed price to net to the same after fees, or (b) provide an off-market credit/invoice adjustment. Both require documenting in the SOW. Example calc: `customer_price = target_net / (1 - marketplace_fee)` — so $90k net with 12% fee => list ~$102,272.

Marie - DealDesk: Also remember contract commitments: marketplace private offers are tied to the marketplace account and billing entity. If the customer wants a Redwood invoice (for their internal PO process) instead of marketplace invoice, that's a different flow and likely needs enterprise billing enabled. Which does the customer want?

Sam (AM): They said they prefer marketplace invoice so procurement can auto-sync. Their procurement team sometimes refuses off-market credits. I can ask if they're willing to accept a marketplace private offer.

Markus - Marketplace Ops: We can create the private offer and set the price. Need: (1) customer marketplace account ID, (2) SKU mapping (POC SKU vs standard SKU), (3) effective dates. Note: some customers' procurement systems won't accept recurring marketplace metering invoices — they demand a PO up front. Marketplace does not accept POs in many cases. If they require a PO, we may have to do a direct deal (not marketplace).

Ajay (SE): POC acceptance criteria I proposed to Acme: "SLA: 99.9% inference availability for POC window; throughput target 200 qps; latency p95 < 300ms for 2k context". If we do private offer, add a clause: 'POC reserved capacity will be provided for the duration and will not auto-renew.'

Lia Finance: If we proceed via marketplace private offer, we need to forecast recognized revenue and confirm tax handling. Also need to check if their reseller agreement changes fee split. Please add expected ARR and discount percent to the thread.

Sam (AM): Expected commit for POC -> convert scenario: $120k first-year ARR if they convert. They want 20% off list.

Marie - DealDesk: 20% off + marketplace fees will likely reduce net > threshold we require for approval. I'll start a Deal Desk case. @Lia Finance can you flag revenue impact and whether we can accept a slightly smaller net discount to preserve margin?

Lia Finance: On it. Quick estimate: 20% off list plus 12% marketplace fee => net ~ (0.8 * list) * (0.88) = 0.704 * list. We need net >= target margin. Send me the list SKU & price.

Markus - Marketplace Ops: One more procurement constraint: some customers require that billing be in their home country ledger. Marketplace region must match. If Acme is in EU and wants EU billing entity, we need the EU marketplace listing or an EU-managed private offer. That adds lead time (3-5 business days).

Sam (AM): Got it. I'll ask Acme for their marketplace account ID and whether EU invoicing is required.

Marie - DealDesk: Next steps I propose: 1) Sam to confirm marketplace account ID + EU billing requirement, 2) Ajay to attach POC SKU config + timeframe, 3) Lia to run margin calc and pre-approve net discount band, 4) I open deal-desk case for private-offer approval + legal to review special terms (no-auto renew clause, upgrade path).

Ajay (SE): Attaching quick config here (paste):
```
POC-SKU: redwood-dedicated-poc
Capacity: 8x A100-equivalent vGPUs
Duration: 14 days (start date TBD)
Price: TBD (use marketplace private offer price)
```

Marie - DealDesk: I'll need the final proposed list price to submit. If possible add a fallback: if Marketplace private offer can't be executed within 10 business days, fallback to direct invoice with same net economics and credit memo to align billing. Legal will need to sign off on that fallback.

Sam (AM): I'll chase Acme now. ETA customer reply ~48h. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Marketplace Bot: private_offer_created? No — awaiting account ID from sales.

Marie - DealDesk: Tagging this thread `dealdesk/private-offer` in our tracker once we have the list price.
